page_title: LogoLight: turn off or dim the MacBook Pro's glowing Apple logo

summary.name: LogoLight
summary.one_liner: A free, open-source macOS menu bar app that turns off, dims, or animates the illuminated Apple logo on the back of the OLED MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display.
use_cases: Turning off the glowing Apple logo on the lid of an OLED MacBook Pro
Dimming the illuminated logo to a set brightness
Animating the logo with breathe, pulse, or heartbeat effects
Syncing the logo glow to music
Toggling the logo from the menu bar or Control Center
summary.what_it_does: LogoLight is a menu bar app for the illuminated Apple logo on the MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display. It can switch the logo off, set its brightness with a slider, and run effects (Breathe, Pulse, Heartbeat) or a music-driven glow. The menu shows a live view of the lid in space black or silver. It can be toggled from Control Center or by Option-clicking the menu bar icon, and it can launch at login. Usually no password is needed; if direct control fails, it asks for the administrator password once to install a sudoers rule that allows only the two Apple logo on/off commands. Other Macs open the app but report the logo as unavailable.
notable: Free and open source under the MIT license, source on GitHub
Signed with Developer ID and notarized by Apple
Brightness and effects available; Apple's Terminal method only supports on/off
Live menu view that reads the lid's state from hardware
caveats: Only works on the MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display; other Macs show the logo as unavailable
Not on the Mac App Store because store sandboxing blocks the required system interfaces
Brightness and effects need direct control; if that is unavailable, only on/off works, after a one-time admin password prompt
